confidence_rationale: Step 7 rubric, HIGH row: every declared test either ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code observed in this run. No MEDIUM trigger fired -- no command test was refused, no coverage-gap exclusion was needed for any of the six metadata types present, and check-outputs reported no missing, empty or malformed declared output. No LOW trigger fired -- every declared checker resolved to exactly one existing script, the artefact directory holds 13 files, and every exit code was captured to tests/M1-S01/.

process_observations.observation: The CompactLayout member-form gap the prior test run (2026-09-09T19-52-47Z) flagged as concerning is now closed rather than merely patched around. That run found the manifest's bare Case_Intake member disagreed with the object-qualified Case.Case_Intake the mock deploy's --source-dir derivation produced, and deploy-order.md called it the manifest's thinnest grounding. Rebuild #3 rewrote package.xml to the object-qualified form, admin/list-views-and-compact-layouts was bumped to v1.2.0 with rules CL-MEM-01 (ERROR on a bare enumerated CompactLayout/ListView member) and CL-MEM-02, and this run's declared checker now enforces the same form it exercises, not merely a form the mock deploy happened to prefer.

Rebuild #3 was surgical and self-documented at the metadata-builder run record: 'package.xml CompactLayout member Case_Intake -> Case.Case_Intake (object-qualified); ... all other 12 artefacts byte-identical (sha256)'. This run's own manifest and xml checks corroborate that scope: the only content difference visible from artefacts on disk versus the prior test run is the single CompactLayout member string in package.xml.

Per this run's own instruction, the manifest derivation this agent's AGENT.md documents (Step 3, citing devops/salesforce-dx-project-structure's generic source-format mapping) does not itself state that a CompactLayout member must be object-qualified -- that rule lives one level down, in admin/list-views-and-compact-layouts' checker and references, which is not in step-tester's own Mandatory Reads (it is read only because this step's plan.json cites it as a checker). This run applied the object-qualified form as the correct one because CL-MEM-01/02 and the checker's own exit code say so, and the manifest test still reads consistent -- recorded here as a tester-logic note, not a step failure, per this run's explicit instruction.

build_plan.py emitted three WARNs on unrelated steps while writing this status transition -- M5-S02 acceptance_tests[0], M5-S04 acceptance_tests[0] and [3] each declare a checker with a non-standard argument form that step-tester will run verbatim. They did not affect M1-S01 and are the known unconverged-checker-flag follow-up in standards/build-orchestration.md section 5, unchanged since the prior run's note on this.

Manual test 1's counter-example text is still stale as of this run, unchanged from the prior test cycle: it reads 'the BARE process name (not Case.Support Process)', a form the businessProcess fix (F-11, rebuild #2) already superseded. The assertion it guards still holds against the artefacts on disk. Neither this agent nor build-step-runner may edit a plan field beyond its own status transition.
M1-S01 is tested and its documentation predates rebuild #3.
